one_line: Film one unbroken shot of the product doing its thing, with the one comment-word ask on screen from frame one.

q1_hook.what: 0:00 front view of a pink robot with a pen on a white table, an avocado card on its head. Text from frame one: "הרובוט שמצייר לבד" / "רוצה לינק?" / "כתבי "רובוט" בתגובות". First line drawn at 0:03.
q1_hook.why: A toy that moves a pen by itself poses a clear "what will it draw?" that the Reel answers line by line (H5). Topic and ask are in text at 0:00, with no intro (H1, T3). No person speaks, but music keeps sound on (H4, H6). The product is already working (S1).

beats.what: Robot with an avocado card on its head, pen at the paper; three-line text box
beats.why: Topic and comment-word ask before anything moves

beats.what: The pen draws an avocado outline in rings by itself
beats.why: The pen moving alone is the visual curiosity

beats.what: New card (balloon) at 0:11, then an apple tree at 0:14; each drawn in turn
beats.why: A new card and drawing every 3 to 12 s

beats.what: Snail card at 0:26; spiral, body, then a smiling face at 0:37
beats.why: The cutest drawing arrives last in the take

beats.what: Handheld cuts: marker cases, four outlines, the card stack
beats.why: Shows what comes in the box, 1 s per shot

beats.what: Hand-coloured snail, avocado, balloon and tree
beats.why: The finished result in the last 2 s

q2_flow.interaction_prompts: On screen all the way: "כתבי "רובוט" בתגובות" for a link. Caption: follow the page, tag a friend "שחייבת את זה לילדים שלה", and comment the word "רובוט".
q2_flow.why: Each drawing forming line by line is a small open loop, repeated four times with a new picture each time (H5, R3). One take of 39 s is the proof but has long stretches of the same view (R1, E2). The coloured result arrives at the very end (R4).

q3_cta.what: On screen 0:00 to the end: "רוצה לינק? כתבי "רובוט" בתגובות". Caption: "רוצות לינק לרובוט?" then 1 follow the page, 2 tag a friend, 3 comment "רובוט", and "ואשלח לכן את הלינק בפרטי".
q3_cta.why: One comment word that delivers a real thing, the link, shown from frame one to the end (C3, C6). But the caption adds follow and tag asks, three actions in all (C1), a gate that reads as engagement for its own sake (C2).

q4_shown.what: The robot working from the first frame; four drawings built live in one take (avocado, balloon, apple tree, snail); marker cases and the card stack 0:40-0:43; hand-coloured results 0:43-0:44. No person, no child, no price, no brand name.
q4_shown.why: The product is shown working at 0:00 and the result forms in front of the viewer, the proof a toy needs (S1, F8). No price or age range is given, so the buyer's questions go to the DM (S3). No face or hands is needed because the robot is the performer (S4).

q5_edit.what: One static take 0:00-0:39, then five handheld shots of about 1 s each to 0:45. The card and paper change at 0:11, 0:14 and 0:26; the paper position jumps at 0:14 and 0:26. The text box never changes. Music throughout; ends on the coloured result.
q5_edit.why: A 39 s unbroken take is honest proof that it draws alone but holds the same view for long stretches (R1, E2). A new card every 10 to 12 s adds some news (R3). The fast colour shots deliver the payoff in the last 5 s (R4).

q6_topic.what: A toy robot that draws pictures from cards, with colouring markers, for mothers who want a screen-free activity.
q6_topic.why: Screen-free play touches a real parenting concern, but only the caption says it (K6). The mood is calm and satisfying rather than a high-arousal peak (K1). "Encourages creativity" is a modest claim (K4).

q7_filmed.what: A propped phone, static, front view at table height, the robot filling the middle of the frame, a play kitchen and plush toys behind, daylight. Then handheld high-angle close-ups of markers and drawings on a white table.
q7_filmed.why: A home setting and a fixed phone look native (H8, F7), and live video shows the product moving the whole time (F8). The drawing forms in the bottom third, where the caption and buttons sit (F2). The file is just under 720 pixels wide (F3).

q8_text.on_screen: A three-line box with two small emoji, centred at about 40 to 45% of the frame height, small white type with a dark edge, unchanged from 0:00 to the end, over the card base and the robot's head: "הרובוט שמצייר לבד" / "רוצה לינק?" / "כתבי "רובוט" בתגובות". No other text.
q8_text.caption: "אמהות תראו איזה רובוט גאוני 🤖🎨". About 70 words: contents list, a screen-free benefit, a three-step ask, a DM promise, 3 hashtags including #עליאקספרסישראל. No disclosure words.
q8_text.why: The text states topic and ask at 0:00, and with no speech it carries the message muted (T3, T1). It is short but small and light on a light wall, and it covers the product the whole time (T2, T5). The caption has search words and 3 hashtags (T7); no disclosure is stated (T8).

weak_points: 39 s of one view with the drawing low in the frame; small, low-contrast text that never changes; caption asks for follow, tag and comment; no price, age range or child; no disclosure.
lumebook_takeaway: Prop the phone and film one unbroken top-down shot of hands paging to the name page, with a short text box stating the topic and one comment word.
not_verified: The robot's brand and seller, price and age range. Whether the take is sped up: the paper jumps at 0:14 and 0:26, which suggests hidden cuts. The music track and whether the account may use it (the transcript shows English lyrics about colours). Whether the link earns the creator a commission. Correction to src/coded: the pen touches the paper at 0:00 but the first line appears at 0:03; the take is not one picture, the card changes at 0:11, 0:14 and 0:26.
